This research study presents a comparison of five different supervised machine learning algorithms namely Naive Bayes, Decision Tree, Multilayer Perceptron, Support Vector Machine and Random Forest for the classification of the disease dataset collected from an online repository. The Random Forest algorithm emerges to be the most efficient algorithm in classifying the diseases. Also, the research study applies different attribute selection measures to evaluate the impact of accuracy on the Random Forest classifier empirically. Among the different node splitting criteria, we conclude that the GINI index performed better on average than the Information Gain and Gain Ratio. The work is implemented using the Python 3.7 programming language.

articleTitle: Bridgeless Landsman Converter Based PM-BLDC Motor Drive for Exhaust Fan
abstract: Permanent Magnet Brushless DC machines (PM-BLDCM) are in high demand for many applications. This paper involves the modelling and control of PM-BLDC motor drive for industrial load which includes exhaust fan. For better performance of the complete drive system, a bridgeless landsman converter (BL-Landsman) is modelled and designed for exhaust fan requirement. This configuration consists of LC filter in series with BL-Landsman converter. This converter is operated in discontinuous conduction mode (DCM) of input and output currents. The DC link voltage of the system is controlled using voltage follower approach. The switching losses of the voltage source inverter (VSI) is minimized by low fundamental frequency. This causes cancellation of ripples at load side. Furthermore, Total harmonic distortions (THD) in supply current, ripples in input and output current along with output voltage polarities are compared with several AC-DC converter topologies like, BL-CUK, BL-SEPIC, BL-LUO and BL-ZETA. For the application of exhaust fan, BL-Landsman converter gives good performance. To validate the system performance, MATLAB/SIMULINK platform is used.

articleTitle: Short Term Load Forecasting using Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: With recent technological and scientific advancements in the power systems, there has been a tandem need for load forecasting. This paper mainly discusses short-term load forecasting, which refers to the prediction of the system load demand over an interval ranging between minutes ahead to one week ahead. With advent of Machine Learning, the process of demand prediction has become easier and cost effective. The challenge of predicting the future demand can be characterized as a regression problem, hence the method of Support Vector Regression is used, as it has proved to be a robust method in the recent research. Different Neural Networks are also being used in several domains; hence Deep Neural Network has also been used to test the accuracy, The paper discusses the results obtained by two different methods. The comparison between the outcomes of the different algorithms has been discussed, in order to get a thorough understanding. The methods are explained vastly. The paper also discusses the factors affecting load forecasting directly.

articleTitle: Torsion: Web Reconnaissance using Open Source Intelligence
abstract: Internet technology has made surveillance widespread and access to resources at greater ease than ever before. This implied boon has countless advantages. It however makes protecting privacy more challenging for the greater masses, and for the few hacktivists, supplies anonymity. The ever-increasing frequency and scale of cyber-attacks has not only crippled private organizations but has also left Law Enforcement Agencies(LEA's) in a fix: as data depicts a surge in cases relating to cyber-bullying, ransomware attacks; and the force not having adequate manpower to tackle such cases on a more microscopic level. The need is for a tool, an automated assistant which will help the security officers cut down precious time needed in the very first phase of information gathering: reconnaissance. Confronting the surface web along with the deep and dark web is not only a tedious job but which requires documenting the digital footprint of the perpetrator and identifying any Indicators of Compromise(IOC's). TORSION which automates web reconnaissance using the Open Source Intelligence paradigm, extracts the metadata from popular indexed social sites and un-indexed dark web onion sites, provided it has some relating Intel on the target. TORSION's workflow allows account matching from various top indexed sites, generating a dossier on the target, and exporting the collected metadata to a PDF file which can later be referenced.

articleTitle: Convolution Neural Network-Based Detection in Software Defined Networks
abstract: In recent years, software-defined networking (SDN) has evolved into adaptive emerging network technology. It is both dynamic and manageable. The SDN architecture creates a distinction between the two planes, the control and data plane. The routing and processing resolution of data packets is handled by the control plane whereas the direction to the data packet and its processing is carried out by the data plane based on the conclusions of the results of the control plane in the SDN. The protocol based on the flowing property is known as OpenFlow (OF). This is responsible for the transmission between the control plane in the SDN and its switches. This is a highly competitive field and many open-source software makers are presenting us with a variety of controllers for SDN. Some examples of the same are ONOS, Ryu, and Open daylight. A paradigm shift to using deep learning techniques is seen in the computer world with such techniques being used for extensive research in various fields. Deep learning has given breakthrough results in speech and image recognition. Its use for intrusion detection is gradually starting to increase. Deep learning can be the benchmark for the next generation of intrusion detection by early and more accurate detection of zero-day attacks. Hence, we offer the DL-IDPS (deep learning-enabled intrusion detection and prevention system) over SDN networks in this study using the Convolution Neural Network (CNN). The proposed DL-IDPS is expected to detect the different kinds of attacks possible on any SDN network.

articleTitle: Deep learning based Layout Equivalence Detection in Compressed Domain and analysis of different Document Image Dataset: A Systematic Study
abstract: Use of electronic gadgets is increasing in this digital era as people often tend to use digital devices to perform there day to day activities. More and more fields such as government offices, banking sectors, educational institutions and so on use digital information for ease of storage and access. Today, the world is moving towards the paperless offices than using the physical paper documents. Paper documents once scanned get converted into document images. These document images have complex layouts which make it difficult to process. Processing these document images is a document image analysis problem known as DIA problem. It's been observed that the document image dataset is exponentially increasing which has simple to very complex structure leading to complex problems in processing. In order to find suitable solutions to these issues we intend to make use of a deep learning based approach for layout equivalence detection which can help to solve the retrieval problems and which may also be useful in the area of digital forensics based on the document layouts. Proposed approach follows two stages in which the first stage performs object detection using deep learning model followed by creation of bounding boxes for different entities which is further used to compare the layouts of the document images to predict the matching layouts for equivalence. Proposed model is a combination of object detection, bounding box creation and extraction of layouts which further uses Brute force matcher to perform equivalence detection. Here, we also present the state of the art document image datasets that is widely used by the researchers in the literature for solving DIA problems. Some of the publicly available datasets are considered for analyzing the results. The results show the robustness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Grey Oyster Mushroom Classification toward a Smart Mushroom Grading System for Agricultural Factory
abstract: A visual evaluation of vegetables and fruits helps classify tasks in handling the agricultural product quality. For this, the grey oyster mushroom requires attention for having a smart grading system for helping the agricultural farmers to ease their job in grading them before transporting mushrooms to a supermarket. Mainly in Malaysia, Federal Agricultural Marketing Authority (FAMA) is an agricultural organization that proposed a categorical type for grey oyster mushrooms; premier, grades 1, 2, and 3 based on mushroom's size, color, pattern, and damage condition. Manual eye observation is still conducted in this traditional classification for grey oyster mushrooms. Even though most research works are conducted with the inter-class task for a bigger group of mushroom classification, the intra-class mushroom study is still limited and needs attention, which compares the available image to a smaller level or class. In this paper, intra-class classification, image processing, and deep learning are utilized, with an introduction of grey oyster mushroom classification using CNN as our classification engine is proposed. Here, it is necessary to evaluate the grading system traditionally conducted manually by farmers based on the FAMA guidance. The study also aims to design a grey oyster mushroom classification network model. The VGG16 pre-trained network model will be studied and utilized in this study. This study's results should introduce systematic training, testing, and evaluation for grey oyster mushroom classification for agricultural activities by evaluating the range of possible design solutions utilizing machine learning by a new arrangement of mushroom dataset images. Thus, the research performed a comparative and reliable classification accuracy, although the study is still mid-way to accomplishing the full research target, ready with a smart mushroom grading system for the agricultural factory.

articleTitle: Effect of Organic Acids and Thermal Ageing in Oil-Impregnated Kraft paper used in Power Transformers
abstract: The insulation system in a power transformer is basically comprised of oil and oil-impregnated paper. The lifetime of power transformer is very much dependent on the insulation health. Due to several years of continuous service related stress, the oil-paper insulation degrades. This degradation manifests itself through the generation of moisture and many by-products. One important by product is the formation of organic acids. Presence of acids further accelerates the ageing process of the oil paper insulation. Therefore, understanding the ageing of oil-paper insulation in presence of acidic components in transformer oil becomes very important from asset management point of view. This paper discusses the combined effect of acidified transformer oil and thermal ageing on different important properties of Kraft paper. The properties under investigation are polarization current, dissipation factor and mechanical strength oil impregnated kraft paper. The kraft paper samples were aged for a total 30 days, and the variation of abovementioned properties were studied throughout that period.

articleTitle: Image Segmentation for Self-Driving Car
abstract: Machine learning plays a vital role in making a car autonomous. The machine learning algorithms interpret the surrounding data collected from the car's sensors and camera and perform desired actions. Semantic segmentation is one of the various techniques which can be used in self-driving cars. High computational costs will be needed to obtain higher accuracy in semantic segmentation, which is not suited for embedded systems. So, there is a need to get high accuracy models with low computational requirements. This paper used a U-Net model for the semantic segmentation task, which shows good accuracy. We will be using the cityscape image pair dataset to train and test our model. We will evaluate our model based on the Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve and Intersection over Union (IOU).

articleTitle: Temperature Prognosis Using Regression Techniques
abstract: In present scenario, weather and temperature prediction is considered as one of the most important aspects on daily life basis. Accurate prediction of weather and temperature at the very right time is very important. Nobody knows when and where; the things might go worse naturally. Thus, pre scenario prediction is the key to mark all the key strategies. In this work, temperature prediction is achieved by using multiple well known regression techniques namely Multi Linear Regression (MLR), Polynomial Regression (PR) and Support Vector Regression (SVR). During the implementation of the experiment, it was observed that all the above-mentioned regression techniques came up with almost the similar type of the performance in terms of the accuracy, so to differentiate the performance of each regression technique in detail, the comparison was done on the basis of Mean Square Error (MSE). After the completion of the experiment, it was observed that all the regression techniques came up with a better performance result and the training accuracy achieved of MLR, PR and SVR came out to be 99%, 99.71% and 99.77% respectively whereas talking about the MSE of all three regression techniques came out to be 0.900937, 0.275822 and 2.022358 respectively.

articleTitle: DNA Sequence Classification with Improved Performance of Supervised Classifiers using Nature Inspired Algorithms
abstract: Deoxyribo Nucleic Acid (DNA) is a unique macromolecule of all living species. It passes on the hereditary data of life. Artificial Intelligence can be used to classify the DNA class based on the sequence, as it can reduce the time taken and can enhance the information managing limits compared to a manual technique that is followed for ages. The main objective of this project is to develop a machine learning model that can improve the classification of DNA sequences. Firefly Algorithm (FA), Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO) Algorithm, Bat Algorithm (BA), and Hybrid Bat Algorithm (HBA) were some of the Nature Inspired Algorithms (NIA) have been employed in this research. These NIAs generally follow “Evolutionary Computation”. Six different supervised classifiers are utilized to classify the DNA sequence. This research is a practical survey aimed at identifying the best classifier with the best NIA among the candidates for reliably classifying DNA sequences. With the use of NIAs, all of the classifier's performance has improved, however, GWO's random forest classifier has the highest accuracy of all of the classifiers tested at 97.1 percent.

articleTitle: Exploratory evaluation of the C4.5 and Transfer Learning Algorithms for Breast Cancer Classification
abstract: Breast cancer is proclaimed to be the most prevalent tumor and classification of the tumor cells into Benign and Malignant ascertains to be beneficial in the preparatory stages for the affected patient to receive the optimal treatment. A contrasting comparison is drawn between two algorithms. Machine Learning makes use of the Transfer Learning technique to attain a higher learning rate and stores the knowledge gained whilst classifying the tumor cells. And the contrasting algorithm C4.5 is used in Data Mining as a Decision Tree Classifier which aids in making the most valuable decision on the given set of data and also proves its use by curtailing the conclusive overfitting rate.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Multi-Bit Linear Feedback Shift Register based PRNG with FPGA Implementation using different Primitive Polynomials
abstract: Many applications like Data Encryption keys, secure communication channels, etc that use cryptography make use of Linear Feedback Shift Registers (LFSR) based Pseudo-Random Number Generators (PRNG) as they provide better performance as compared to other counters in terms of hardware, area and speed. This paper focuses on a comparative study of standard and modular multi-bit LFSR based PRNGs with different primitive feedback polynomials using Verilog HDL. An FPGA synthesis has been carried out along with a hardware implementation, to assess which architecture yields the best results.

articleTitle: Prediction of Bipolar Disorder Using Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: bipolar disorder may be an advanced disorder that affects variant individuals across the world. We assume that with the utilization of huge information with machine learning we will facilitate every patient as well as doctors to perform a much better designation of this sickness. Paper aims to use different Machine learning algorithms to predict the variants of bipolar disorder. The prediction model would help the psychiatrists fordiagnosing whether the patients are having a depression or mania episode, or staying in an exceedingly euthymic state. It also aims at developing a prophetic model with an appropriate level of confidence, it's essential to own each associate understanding of the information that's getting used and also thetheory relating to every algorithmic rule that's applied, similarly as having enough information for the algorithms to figure with.

articleTitle: Molles Corde: A Neural Network-based Multi-model System for Detecting Heart Diseases
abstract: In the realm of medicine, diagnosing heart disease has become a difficult undertaking. There is a critical need for early detection of heart problems in order to offer patients proper treatment. A correct diagnosis of cardiac disease leads to the right treatment for the patient. The tremendous advances in the area of Neural Networks and Deep Learning are aimed at developing intelligent systems that assist medical practitioners in disease prediction, detection, and decision-making. The proposed model in the paper, “Molles Corde” (a Latin term meaning “Resilient Heart”, reflecting the desired outcome from effective detection), is a two-staged, multi-model neural network system. The model consists of a level one, basic disease detection model for a surface level detection of the disease and an advanced model, consisting of several neural networks each trained on detection for in depth, specific heart-related disease. The heart diseases detected using this system are Arrhythmia, Hypertension, Coronary Heart Disease (CHD) and Cardiovascular Disease (CVD).

articleTitle: A Inventive Method for Door Detection on FPGA Using Sobel Edge Algorithm
abstract: Now a days door detection is a key factor in robotics, especially physically disabled people or old age or senior citizen. So, it necessary to improve an assistive device for detecting door. The proposed work includes the way of robot is going to identify the door by using Sobel edge detection algorithm through image processing, once the image of the door is captured then robot move inside the door or outside the door as per the requirement. The image will be captured through camera which is fixed to the robot whenever there is an edge like structure while moving from one room to another room. This Sobel edge algorithm is implemented on Xilinx FPGA Zed board with 100Mhz frequency.

articleTitle: Enhancing Supply Chain Management Using Blockchain Technology
abstract: A supply chain is a network of businesses and distribution choices that conducts the tasks of acquiring inputs, transforming these resources into variable and completed outputs, and distributing these manufactured goods to clients. The network is made up of many jobs at varying tiers of operation & distribution alternatives that carry out the work of procurement. It is necessary function in commercial and industrial sectors; nevertheless, the intricacy of the system differs significantly between industries. Blockchain is revolutionizing the modern landscape by providing a fresh viewpoint on access control, resilience, and overall performance. It provides a safe means of exchanging any type of item, service, or trade. Block chain technology would allow for further flexible production networks, quicker breakthroughs, and a somewhat intimate consumer interaction market. Such an article provides an outline of distributed ledger-tech as well as its possibilities for improving logistics operations.

articleTitle: A Multinomial Naïve Bayes Classifier for identifying Actors and Use Cases from Software Requirement Specification documents
abstract: A software Requirements Specification (SRS) document is an NL (Natural Language) written textual specification that documents the functional and non-functional requirements of the system and various expectations of clients in a software development project. To understand the different requirements of the system, developers make use of this SRS document. In this paper, we apply Naive Bayes classifiers - Multinomial and Gaussian over different SRS documents and classify the software requirement entities (Actors and Use Cases) using Machine Learning based methods. SRS documents of 28 different systems are considered for our purpose and we define labels for the entities Actor and Use Case. Multinomial Naive Bayes is a popular classifier because of its computational efficiency and relatively good predictive performance. Out of the classifiers tried out, the Multinomial Naive Bayes recognizes Actors and Use Cases with an accuracy of 91%. Actors and Use Cases can be extracted with high accuracy from the SRS documents using Multinomial Naive Bayes, which then can be used for plotting the Use Case diagram of the system. Automated UML (Unified Modeling Language) model generation approaches have a very prominent role in an agile development environment where requirements change frequently. In this work, we attempt to automate the Requirement Engineering (RE) phase that can improve and accelerate the entire Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC).

articleTitle: Microservices Event Driven and Streaming Architectural Approach for Payments and Trade Settlement Services
abstract: In BFSI (Banking, Finance, Securities and Insurance) industry core day-to-day operations are payment, clearing and settlement (PCS) services are key functions. Having a good PCS system is a must to have a satisfied customers and achieve accelerated growth in revenues. Implementation of PCS transactions processed through a series of integrated systems and integrations were neither real-time nor near real-time. The evolution of Digital Transformation (DT), microservices, containerization, Cloud-native deployments and peer pressure in the BFSI sector has triggered the architecting and development of real-time or near real-time or asynchronous PCS systems against synchronous ones. In the current work, an effort has been made to architect a layered system with an in-built and Event Driven Architecture (EDA) that can handle asynchronous transactions. The intended system has multiple layers like integration, application, data, security, and infrastructure. The new architecture should address a) business concerns like usability, security management, functional coverage, flexibility, functional integration, automation, and reporting, b) technical concerns like modularity, extensibility, reusability, future-readiness, performance, adaptability and c) operational concerns like managibility, maintainability, scalability, availability, cloud and robust enough to handle the load. The goal of current work is achieve a multi-tier event driven and stream processing architecture that consists of front-end, API gateway, microservices, databases and flexible to deploy on a hybrid cloud environment. The system is capable of interfacing with industry standard third party systems.

articleTitle: Design of High Quality Factor Symmetrical Differential Inductor using Intercalated-Graphene
abstract: In this paper, the design of a novel symmetrical differential on-chip inductor using intercalated graphene (a 2D material) for next-generation radio-frequency-integrated-circuit (RFIC) applications is presented. The intercalated graphene provides better conductivity compared to conventional metals like copper (Cu) which results in improved quality(Q)-factor. The proposed symmetrical differential inductor was designed for outer diameter (d<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>) of 170 /µm at 0.18-um CMOS technology. In comparison to traditional inductors, our symmetrical differential inductors based on intercalated graphene have a greater inductance density while achieving high Q-factors of approximately 30 at 11.8GHz frequency. This completely material-enabled method offers an exciting remedy to the long-standing scaling challenge of on-chip inductors, and therefore a possible future for ultra-compact wireless communication systems development.

articleTitle: Multi-level Inverter with Reduced Switch Count and DC Source
abstract: An innovative multilevel inverter is projected in this paper with the integration of packed U cell and level doubling network. The inverter uses a single DC source and two floating capacitors per phase to provide multilevel output voltage. The voltage across capacitors establishes an unequal ratio along with the available de source. The desired voltage of the capacitor is reached with natural balancing of the capacitor without using any sensors and thus the intermediate dc voltage levels are produced. Hence the proposed topology improves the power quality, reduces the switch count, size and cost when compared to another topology. Operation of the circuits verified by simulations in MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Detection of COVID-19 from X-RAY Images using Artificial Intelligence (AI)
abstract: Corona virus (COVID-19) is an infectious disease. Several millions of people worldwide suffer from this disease. The signs of progress of virus infection are more severe damage to lungs and causes to organs failure, death. X-rays are readily available and an excellent alternative method to x-ray imaging in the diagnosis of covid-19 and very crucial role play to recognizing this disease and recovery with hospitalization. The goal of this revise is to expand a reliable method for detecting COVID-19 from digital chest X-ray pictures using well-before deep-learning algorithms while optimizing detection performance. To train and verify, the transfer learning (TL) approach was utilized with the aid of picture extension. Current would be hugely beneficial in this pandemic because the illness severity and the necessity for prevention methods are at odds with available resources.

articleTitle: Fuzzy-Logic Based INC MPPT Method for Photovoltaic Systems
abstract: Nowadays the solar energy is widely used for electricity generation due to technological development. The renewable energy sources must be used for the technology such as electric vehicles in order to reduce the pollution level. So it is important to increase the efficiency and effectiveness of the renewable energy systems. This paper presents a design of a fuzzy logic based variable step size incremental conductance MPPT method for photovoltaic system. The fuzzy inputs are derived from the slope of PV curve of photovoltaic module namely current-voltage ratio and its derivatives. The simulation of the proposed system is designed in MATLAB SIMULINK. The result shows that the proposed MPPT method is able to track accurate MPP with nearly zero oscillations in PV power.

articleTitle: Computational and Adaptive Offloading in Edge/Fog based IoT environments
abstract: Despite the substantial efficiency advancements, today's cloud services and related paradigms need vast amounts of energy and network, and this demand is only expected to grow. One of the main research questions is whether and how transitioning to edge computing may help reverse this trend. Simulations play a vital role in research since real-world deployments of edge or fog infrastructure are infrequent. In this research, we look at how to use a range of simulation tools to help with computation-intensive offloading in edge networks. This paper aims to determine the average energy consumption of compute nodes, as well as network traffic and applications, over experimental edge-based networks using an adaptive offloading approach and a blend of analytical and precisely defined modeling tools.

articleTitle: Vaccine Cold Storage Monitoring and Tracking using LoRaWAN
abstract: This paper proposes a methodology for a cold storage monitoring and tracking system built upon a LoRa network. The architecture comprises an end node with a monitoring system, a LoRaWAN Gateway, LORIOT network server and the user application. The end node has built-in temperature, pressure and humidity sensors. Force-Sensitive-Resistors and a GPS module are interfaced externally to the module. The monitoring system can thereby measure the parameters inside the chamber as well as track the chamber in real time. Further, the presence of vaccines is detected using the force-sensitive-sensors. A web application has been designed to provide the user with an interface to analyse the network parameters, receive data from the end node, issue signals to the end node and track the cold storage during transportation.

articleTitle: Speech Emotion Recognition
abstract: Emotions play a vital role in identifying a human's mental state. Emotions are the way to express one's outlook and mental state to others. In this paper, an analysis of speech [8] to extract the emotions has been done. The feature vector comprises components of the audio signal that portray specific features of the speaker, such as tone, pitch, and energy, which is significant to prepare the classifier model to precisely recognize a particular emotion. Extraction of Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients(MFCC) [3] has been done from the speech signals to create the dataset for the research work. The feature vector extracted in the training dataset is then sent to the classifier model. The test dataset will go through the extraction technique, following which the classifier would settle on a choice concerning the hidden feeling in the test audio. As a part of dataset preparation, four different datasets(i.e., SAVEE, RAVDESS, TESS, CREMA-D) have been used. Support vector machines [4], LSTM, random forests and CNN model have been used in this study for classifying emotions. 2D CNN outperformed all the other models by giving an accuracy of nearly 70% on the testing dataset.

articleTitle: A Project on Statistical Analysis, ETL Automation, and Intelligence Reporting
abstract: The integration of data visualization and data analytics has been rising rapidly. Companies working on a large scale have a tremendous amount of data, this data has huge potential and can be used in order to improve the functioning of such an organization. The data can be used to optimize various areas of the organization, improvement of products, giving a better customer experience, increasing efficiency and much more. There has been an increase in the amount of tools and solutions created for working with data. The end result is produced by the combination of various technologies. A data pipeline can consist of data visualization tools, Machine learning models, Cloud database management systems etc. Our paper provides a case study on how we used a data pipeline in order to streamline the data and optimize the selection process of such a large scale organization. The Teach for India Fellowship program is an opportunity for India's brightest and most promising youth, from the nation's best institutes, to serve as full-time teachers to students from low-income communities in under-resourced schools. For the selection of these students Teach for India has a selection model in place which weeds out a certain percentage of applicants. These applicants are then reviewed by a special set of reviewers at Teach for India. Our project aims at providing a better understanding of the different competencies that are taken under consideration during the selection process and link them to the fellow's performance in the institute. The methodology and the approach can be used for many such organizations having nation wide data and requires finding the relationship between two groups of data and wants to optimize their selection process.

articleTitle: Data Augmentation for Brain Tumor Segmentation using MONAI Framework
abstract: In 2020, worldwide 308,102 brain and nervous system cancer cases were reported out of which 251,329 deaths were registered i.e. ≈ 82.0 % fatality rate [1] and glioma was found to be one of most occurring brain tumors in the world, and it can be both benign or metastatic, and because of the high heterogeneity present in the occurrence of the lesion in terms of size, location and histology combined with the limitation of expert annotated dataset and programming frameworks for the development of automatic segmentation systems using deep learning presents a need of having an efficient and robust data augmentation pipeline to significantly boost the generalization capabilities of automatic segmentation systems based on deep neural network models. In this work, the main focus was on the development of a data augmentation pipeline, and a design is proposed using MONAI open-source domain specialized python framework, which can later be leveraged to train various U-Net based architectures in the context of the BraTS-2020 dataset without using any external multi-modal brain MRI dataset.

articleTitle: Text Categorization of Telugu News Headlines
abstract: The era of digitization has generated huge amounts of data in every field in the range of petabytes, and the news is one of them. To adopt a classification technique using only human intervention is impossible and also like many other Indian languages, the Telugu language is belonging to the Dravidian family which is rich in morphological content. While Natural Language Processing deals with the textual format of data, different types of word embedding features are considered and passed to the models. Existing work on this problem statement is accomplished only with count-based algorithm word embeddings. In this study, several methods were performed to obtain the best model for categorization of the newspaper articles. These methods include building custom-based Machine Learning and Deep Learning models with both count and prediction based word embeddings.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Analysis of a Portable VPN Backed By a Machine Learning Firewall
abstract: In today's day and age, the majority of people travel for either work or pleasure, may it be to another city, state, country or even to a local coffee shop. Most people tend to make use of free public wifi available while we are on the go without taking into consideration the risk and vulnerable position that they are placing themselves and their information in without checking to see if these public open WiFis are secure and safe to use or if they have been tampered with and their confidential information is being illegally accessed. In our proposed system, we have created a portable VPN that our devices connect to which sends the data to our home network where the network connection is first scanned in order to detect any malicious activity and warn us against using an unsecured access point.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Transfer Learning CNN for Face Recognition
abstract: The practice of identifying people by looking at their faces is known as face recognition (FR). This technology is frequently used in biometric authentication, surveillance technologies, security systems, law enforcement, real-time attendance systems, smart cards, and other applications. The face recognition technology works in two stages. First, a method for picking up or extracting face characteristics is applied, followed by pattern categorization. Deep learning has lately made important contributions to face recognition technology, particularly the convolutional neural network (CNN). Deep learning employs numerous processing layers to develop data representations with varying degrees of feature extraction. Since the achievements of DeepFace and DeepID, this developing technology has altered the study landscape of facial recognition. Deep learning has dramatically improved cutting-edge performance and aided in the development of effective real-world applications. This study examines the performance of three among the most popular CNN architectures for face recognition. In the proposed work, transfer learning is used to deploy pre-trained CNN models for face recognition such as VGG16, ResNet-50, and MobileNet. Training and validation accuracy and loss were utilized as criterion to enhance the performance of the CNN algorithm. 5 Celebrity Faces Dataset from Kaggle, as well as a local dataset, were used to train and test the models. Face recognition was implemented in two ways: static and webcam-based. The models developed for this research can be used in real-time attendance and surveillance systems.

articleTitle: Implementation of Self Repair Embedded SRAM Using Selectable Redundancy
abstract: In embedding RAM, built in self repair (BISR) is a successful method to improve the yeild. In this work popular march algorithm for memory testing is implemented using a BISR architecture in Modelsim. The BISR architecture is able to eliminate repeat storing of flaws in embedded RAM. Moreover,performance of the BISR for march c- and march ss are compared. This proposed technique is a cost-effective BISR strategy that only stores each defect address once. The presented BISR occupies 20% of the space and can operate at 150MHz.

articleTitle: Lane and Vehicle Detection Using Hough Transform and YOLOv3
abstract: Object tracking at dark is critical to minimizing the number of nocturnal traffic crashes. This paper presents a deep convolutional neural network dubbed M-YOLO to enhance the precision of nocturnal object recognition and to be suited for limited contexts (also including microcontrollers in automobiles). To begin, track line images are separated into other * 2S panels based on the features of uneven spatial and temporal dispersion densities. Additionally, the sensor frequency has been limited to four measurement levels, making it even more suited for tiny source localization, like lateral distance measurement. Thirdly, to optimize the connectivity, a fully connected layer throughout the basic Yolo v3 method is reduced by 53 to 49 levels. Lastly, characteristics like cluster center radius and backpropagation are enhanced.

articleTitle: Synchronization of a Hyperchaotic System with fully unknown parameters via Adaptive Hybrid Control
abstract: This manuscript studies the synchronization and anti-synchronization between two identical hyperchaotic systems having unknown parameters, suggesting the coexistence of adaptive hybrid synchronization behaviour. The controller design is based on the theory of Lyapunov stability so that designed controllers achieve the global asymptotic stability in master-slave configuration. For unknown parameters, adaptive control laws as well as parameter update algorithm are derived, reducing any influence of uncertainty. Hybrid synchronization is highly effective in maintaining the secrecy of communication by using control theory approach. To verify the efficacy of the designed controller, numerical simulations are carried out for two similar hyperchaotic systems.

articleTitle: Sensitive Lesions and Tumour Detection in Brain using Deep Convolutional Neural Network
abstract: A brain tumour is an abnormal development of abnormal brain cells that causes harm to the blood vessels and neurons of the human body. The two forms of brain tumours are benign and malignant. It is vital to diagnose a brain tumour early in order to save the life of someone who is in danger. According to research conducted in the United Kingdom, only approximately 15 persons out of 100 will be able to survive for ten years or longer after being recognised. Because of the advent of Artificial Intelligence, Deep Learning models are now being utilised to identify brain cancers using Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) images. MRI is a type of scanning method that uses high magnetic fields and radio waves to obtain detailed pictures of the interior body. The notion of Transfer Learning and Residual Networks were employed in the suggested work. The model utilised is a classification task that uses MRI images to determine whether or not a tumour is present. We may use the same transfer learning techniques to precisely pinpoint the tumour once it has been found. We utilised several optimizers in Resnet-50 to see how our model responds to changes in optimization strategies. Our suggested model has accuracy with Amsgrad optimizer compared with Adam optimizer, demonstrating improved robustness over the state-of-the-art techniques.

articleTitle: Junctionless TFET Based SRAM for Low Power Applications
abstract: Scaling down the size of the transistors introduce many issues like short channel effect (SCE), drain-induced barrier lowering (DIBL), etc. This may increase the leakage power in the mixed-signal design of circuits. Many novel devices have been proposed to overcome these issues that could suppress SCE to a greater extent. One such novel device is the Junctionless Tunnel field-effect transistor (JLTFET) which combines the advantages of Junctionless FET (JLFET) and Tunnel FET (TFET). In this work, JLTFET with 20 nm technology is proposed and its symbol is generated in cadence virtuoso. The various topologies of SRAM like 6T, 7T, 8T, 9T, and 10T are constructed and their logical operations are verified. For all of these circuits, power dissipation, propagation delay, and static noise margin (SNM) are extracted. It can be seen that 6T performs better in terms of propagation delay and power dissipation whereas 10T excels in its performance in SNM.

articleTitle: Deep Neural Network based Forecasting of Short-Term Solar Photovoltaic Power output
abstract: Renewable energy integration to the conventional power grid is a challenge and requires an accurate forecasting of power output from the renewable energy sources for ensuring the reliability and grid stability. Many forecasting techniques for different time horizons were developed using different machine learning techniques. In the recent past mostly forecasting techniques based on artificial neural networks were developed. But, looking at the environmental parameters like insolation, temperature, sky clearness index and cloud cover etc., and its variable behavior makes the forecasting more complex. To address., complex and non-linearity issues in many applications, deep neural networks were proved effective and hence an attempt made in this paper forecasting power from solar photovoltaic plant for very short-term durations through deep neural networks model and compared the same with ANN model with only one hidden layer and found significant improved accuracy in deep neural networks.

Author Keywords: short term forecast and photovoltaic power output

articleTitle: A framework for IoT-based Resource Scheduling in the Cloud
abstract: Scheduling the resources is a fundamental part of the cloud environment. The facilitation of an efficient scheduling approach is a challenging issue. An ideal resource allocation framework that utilizes square-fuzzy methodology and radial basis function network (RBFN) is discussed here. The main motive of this model is to reduce communication and computation costs. The sensor devices in the IoT sensor layer are clustered initially. Further, the sensor data gathered by cluster heads are transferred to the fog layer. The network traffic is optimized through the fuzzy technique. The energy consumption of the network is reduced by the fog layer and then the data is transferred to the cloud where essential attributes of the cloud server and input are used for scheduling of resources by utilizing modified RBFN. The proposed methodology is analyzed and compared with existing models.

articleTitle: Microstrip Patch Antenna Using Coconut Coir Substrate and its Comparison with FR4 Based Antenna
abstract: In the field of antenna design, there is always a need for alternatives that help to reduce the overall production cost without compromising the performance. The substrate selection is a significant step in the design and manufacturing of an antenna. The most widely used substrates for the antenna are FR4, Duroid, Roger 4350, and Bakelite. Depending on the application of antenna, FR4 is comparatively economical among the four. This paper aims to design a microstrip patch antenna using coconut coir substrate and compares its performance with FR4 based microstrip antenna at 2.4 GHz. With its flexible and robust nature, nano cellulose from coconut coir can be used as an alternative to low dielectric substrates (dielectric < 4) due to the economic and environmental advantages.

articleTitle: SOC Control of Lithium–Ion Battery Using Fuzzy Logic Controller and PID Controller Employed in DC Micro Grid
abstract: Integrating solar panels in DC micro grid is a big task, since it involves a battery for power storage and battery controller. The most tedious task is enhancement of battery life and efficiency. This paper introduces two separate models of DC micro grid, one regulated by fuzzy logic controller and the other one by a conventional PID controller. The fuzzy logic controller is implemented in MATLAB Simulink based upon Mamdani inference system. MPPT, fuzzy logic controller, lithium-ion battery and DC load are all integrated in one Simulink model. Best possible rule base is developed to regulate power flow through the DC micro grid, thus simultaneously enhancing the performance of lithium-ion battery. The fuzzy logic controller facilitates maintenance of SOC of lithium-ion battery within desired limits, which results in prevention of overcharging and over discharging. Also, conventional PID controller is implemented in MATLAB Simulink for maintaining SOC of lithium-ion battery within desired limits. This model involves integration of PID controller, MPPT, bi-directional DC-DC converter and lithium-ion battery. Based upon the obtained performance and results of both Simulink models, a comparison between the two controllers is deduced and corresponding results are analyzed. Transient response analysis is performed to compare the two controllers.

articleTitle: Effect of Various Parameter Variation on Analog/RF Performance of SiGe based Nanowire TFET
abstract: Complementary metal oxide semiconductor (CMOS) FET are continuing to scale up, which significantly improve the energy efficiency and portability of electronic gadgets such as smart phones, has been driven by logical devices with ultra-low power consumption and great performance. Researchers and scientists have devised a number of techniques for reducing MOSFET leakage current in order to make gadgets that are smaller and faster. Nanowire structure is presently being considered as a feasible choice for next analytical device generation because of its extremely-low off-state leaking current when compared to FinFET. However, the off-state current voltage of nanowires has yet to be completely realised. A new Semiconductor on Insulator (SOIGAA) nanowire has been come with up, studied, and simulated thoroughly and systematically using 2D numerical modelling in this study. Oxide thickness, temperature fluctuations, and with and without a core insulator are all compared. The device's low power and energy efficiency make it a good contender for future low-power and energy-efficient products. The non-local BTBT, e- concentration, h+ concentration, electric field, potential, and transfer characteristics of the device are all investigated.

Author Keywords: SOIGAA(Semiconductor on Insulator gate all around)

articleTitle: Business Resiliency for Enterprise Blockchain Payment Systems
abstract: This document explains about technical solution that can be used during disaster situation for financial workloads that use Blockchain for transactions. Blockchain is a highly secure, trusted technology with decentralized, distributed transaction handling capability. Disaster causes outages to entire Blockchain nodes and enterprise workloads. Disaster recovery at the backup geo location helps to continue Blockchain nodes and enterprise workloads. After unplanned disasters, it is not possible to have completely synchronized consistent data copy on the target site, when distance is longer between geo locations. This solution uses predictive analysis on different rolling disaster failure events using Machine learning or Deep learning techniques and does a planned recovery with VM Recovery Manager for DR product (Geographically Dispersed Resiliency) before unplanned outages, so that target site will have complete data copy and brings up Blockchain nodes and enterprise workloads. Planned recovery helps to drain all production site data to the target site gracefully, hence target site will have consistent synchronized copy. Solution provides technical aspects with IBM power hardware and Predictive analysis for Blockchain to continue enterprise workloads without data loss during disaster.

articleTitle: A Simplified Approach to Closed Loop Control of A Non-Isolated Bidirectional DC To DC Converter
abstract: This paper aims at implementing a smart., light weight and economical DC to DC converter topology in closed loop mode in order to design an uninterrupted power supply to the electronic and auxiliary loads in a More Electric Aircraft with high efficiency and good transient and steady state response. The proposed topology uses a non-isolated cascaded bidirectional DC to DC converter which can be used in buck as well as boost mode. The aircraft load which is to be supplied with DC power is so connected that it can take power from AC generator mounted on the engine shaft as well as from an auxiliary battery which gets connected to the load in case the engine gets overloaded due to takeoff., landing or turbulence conditions. The changeover between these two sources happens automatically and appropriate gate signals are provided to the semiconductor switches in the DC to DC converter with the help of closed loop control consisting of PI voltage controller hysteresis current controller. The system performance is tested under randomly varying load conditions and the load voltage and current waveforms are compared against their respective reference values. The system transient response is evaluated in terms of overshoot and voltage regulation across the load. PI controllers can be replaced with more advanced controllers like sliding mode controller or fuzzy controller in order to get even better system response in terms of load current overshoot under changing load conditions.

articleTitle: Modeling and Evaluation of Cascaded Mach Zehnder Modulators for Multi-band Chirped Radar Signal Generation and IF Signal Detection
abstract: The cascaded configuration of Mach-Zehnder Modulators (MZMs) can generate multiple short optical pulses. This configuration can be used as an optical pulse source for various applications including radar systems. In this work, we are proposing a method in which these pulses are used as a radar reference signal that plays an important role in the generation of radar transmit signal and detection of Intermediate Frequency (IF) signals during reception. The repetition rate and number of frequency comb lines are controlled by adjusting the frequency of external input signal applied to the MZMs and the cascading stages. As per the operational frequency requirement of the radar system, the suitable comb components are selected to generate the required RF transmit signal. During receive operation, the same frequency comb component will be used for the detection of IF signal. This paper includes various results of cascaded MZM configuration with changes in RF input frequency, number of cascaded stages and its application results obtained during generation and detection processes. The work is supported with a mathematical analysis which is in compliance with modeling results. The same architecture is extended for the generation of multiband chirped RF signals with centre frequencies at 6.5 GHz (C-band) and 9.5 GHz (X-band) and for the retrieval of respective IF signals.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of WSN using Efficient PSO Approach
abstract: Sensors in wireless sensor networks respond to natural variables such as temperature, strain, moisture, and smoke. The power supply is the greatest restriction in remote sensor organizations. Sensor nodes need to use less power utilization. In distant sensor networks, sensor hubs are employed, with each hub containing a CPU, receiving wire, and battery. Since batteries devour power, some advancement methods are expected to diminish power utilization, so battery life should be broadened. In this paper, we implemented a Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) using different functions like Ackley, Rastrigin, Quadratic Noise, Rosenbrock, and sphere function to optimize power which is a streamlining technique that is propelled by lessening the power utilization of sensor hubs.

articleTitle: A Truthful Decision Making for Divorces Using Data Mining Techniques
abstract: Divorce rates are increasing around the world. During the procedure of divorce, the couple is under a lot of emotional and mental strain. Moreover, divorce also has social and economic ramifications. Considering these points, it is important to examine and analyze the divorce phenomenon. To reduce and prevent the occurrence of future divorce cases, it is very crucial to know what are the factors which lead a couple to divorce. In our proposed work, we have primarily used four classification algorithms namely Naive Bayes, Random Forest, KNN, and GLM then further applied the data mining technique of MCA on KNN and GLM to improve the performance of divorce prediction. The models were evaluated based on Leave-One-Out-Cross-Validation (LOOCV). We have been able to achieve the least test error of 0.58% with GLM + MCA and KNN + MCA.

articleTitle: A Portable Wireless Sleep Monitor System Using My RIO 1900
abstract: Sleep is one of the utmost fundamental components of human life. Low-quality sleep can harm one's health, thus it's important to avoid undesirable sleeping postures linked to personal health issues to get a good night's sleep. Even after getting the recommended amount of sleep, one can wake up in pain, discomfort, and drowsiness. This is primarily related to a poor sleeping posture. However, most existing sleep monitoring systems only provide quantitative data on sleep patterns and length at each sleep stage, rather than focusing on the impact sleep has on sleep quality. The proposed work created a sleep position tracking system that properly records sleep poses. By changing the position of the sleep, the system, which consisted of myRIO setup using LabVIEW IDE, was able to examine the mechanism of the sleep poses effects. According to our testing results, the recommended method efficiently and reliably classifies four SP motions for tracking sleep poses, sleep motion data generated using myRIO accelerometer sensing, and four sleep pose (SP) motions from four sleep posture. As a result, it serves as a critical component in the development of complete sleep-related applications.

articleTitle: Improving Routing System in Vehicular Ad Hoc Network using Real Time Vehicular Traffic Information on City Roads
abstract: Vehicle ad-hoc network is an intelligent transport system. We investigate trifles of the ad-hoc networking system and discovered there are a number of inconclusive issues that could lead to the network collapse. In this paper we tried to ameliorate the road management system and solve the traffic jam issue in real time. VANET applications enable vehicles to connect to the internet to obtain real time news, traffic and weather reports. In real-time VANET is a scheme system, where assorted volatile vehicles and connecting devices come in concretion with a wireless medium. Vehicle to vehicle (V2V) communication is a wireless network, which exchange information about the speed and location of contiguous vehicles, shows great assurance to help fudge accidents, diminish traffic congestion and flourish the ambience. Recent studies have showed that routing protocols may redact on vehicle networks developed using dynamic road traffic information for select the most suitable forwarding path or node.

articleTitle: Dynamic Voltage Restorer for Power Quality Enhancement with Improved Efficiency using Artificial Neural Networks
abstract: Dynamic Voltage Restorer (DVR) is an ideal series compensator used in power systems to eliminate voltage variations. With advanced and modern technologies being implemented in today's power systems, the power quality issues like voltage sags, swells, harmonics, and unbalance occur. The Dynamic Voltage Restorer (DVR) is utilized to counter these issues with numerous control techniques. The DVR is implemented in MATLAB/Simulink with Proportional Integral (PI) Controller and with an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) based Controller. This research aims to improve the efficiency of DVR by the application of an Artificial Neural Network. The proposed method with ANN controller is found to give better results as compared to the conventional PI controller based technique.

articleTitle: Semantic Web Rule Based Decision Support System: Knowledge Graph
abstract: Recently, ontology has been constructed for information retrieval effectively from huge databases. Ontology shows the relationship of information. It is used to share, reuse and exchange domain knowledge to construct new ontology. Semantic web helps to solve the problem of semantic interoperability. The institution organizes a number of activities for student placement such as workshops, conferences, expert sessions, etc. The semantic web rule based decision support system ontology is constructed to predict students placement. First of all the data is collected from students. Next, the collected data is preprocessed. The J48 algorithm is used to classify the data. Further, the Expectation Maximization (EM) algorithm has been taken to form a cluster of classified data. Decision tree has been constructed using the J48 algorithm. Semantic web rules are constructed from a decision tree. The ontology is constructed in Protégé 5.5.0 and semantic web rules are added. Lastly, knowledge graphs of constructed systems have been graphically presented using VOWL, OntoGraf, OntoViz. This system will be helpful to the institute and students to track progress of placement.

articleTitle: Near Threshold Voltage Operation of Error Resilient Dual Edge Triggered Flip Flop
abstract: As we approach towards Near Threshold Voltage Region, we see the dominant effect of PVT Variations in the working of the Circuit. To cope with this problem generally, guard bands are used to counter these effects. But the downside of these guard bands is more power consumption or limiting the performance of the circuit. To minimize these effects Error Detection and Correction logic can be implemented. In this paper, we have implemented two designs of Error Resilient Dual edge-triggered flip flops which utilize the Error Correcting Logic to counter the effects of PVT Variations without having a significant effect on Power and Performance. These designs are implemented in 65nm CMOS Process Node and operated at Near Threshold Voltage Region. Power, Delay, and Monte Carlo analyses are performed on these designs for a wide PVT range to verify the robustness of the design and also evaluate its performance.

articleTitle: MPPT Algorithms with LCL Filter for Grid Connected PV System
abstract: The sum of all harmonic components of a waveform relative to the fundamental component of waveform is termed as total harmonic distortion (THD). In this paper we have compared THD of photovoltaic (PV) systems connected with a grid for four different MPPT algorithms which includes artificial neural network (ANN), incremental conductance (INC), perturb and observe (P&O), and fuzzy logic control (FLC). The simulation results clearly present the difference in THD among all four MPPT algorithms. We have also designed a three phase LCL filters to filter out the harmonics in the output signal of the system. These are the specially designed filters to eliminate the harmonics with improved performance as well as it is cost effective and are smaller in size because of lesser values of inductor and capacitors in it.

articleTitle: Measuring Consumer Perception for P2P Platform: NLP Approach
abstract: The pandemic has forced lenders and borrowers to switch to alternative borrowing., investment solutions. This research explores the Google reviews of users of four P2P lending platforms in India. To understand user sentiments and emotions about P2P lending platforms. The researchers has analysed user sentiments using Vader and Liu Hu methods and defined the polarity as positive or negative sentiment. Further., Plutchik”s wheel of emotions was used to relate with the emotions expressed by the users. A purposeful random sampling method was used to select only 4 out of 21 registered P2P lending platforms based on their date of incorporation. The research also defined a framework for carrying out the sentiment analysis process for this study. The overall results showed that 75.51 % of users had positive sentiments., whereas., only 19.35% of users had negative sentiments about the P2P lending platforms. As most of the reviews posted were from the borrower”s., emotion of joy was seen in all 4 platforms., followed by emotions of sadness., surprise., anger., disgust., and fear.

articleTitle: Design Methods in Nanotechnology Using Quantum Dot Cellular Automata (QCA)
abstract: Quantum Dot Cellular Automata is the extension of CMOS technology. In CMOS technology further scaling down is not possible. QCA is the solution for it and overcomes the drawbacks in CMOS. This paper gives the evaluation of sequential circuit designs and techniques used to design flip flop. This will help the researchers to compare, combine and innovate other ways to further improve the parameters like cell count, device density, delay and energy dissipation. This paper gives comparison of methods used to design flip flops and the best among them. D FF designed using traditional Majority gate or rotated three input majority gate gives optimized result in terms of cells, area and clock cycle. It makes use of just 20 cells, 0.02µm2 area and 1 clock cycle. QCADesigner version 2.0.3 software and QCADesinger E is used to verify the simulation results in QCA. Further optimization and digitalization is possible by improving the parameters and by making use of innovative methods.

articleTitle: Techno-Economic Analysis of Renewable Energy Resources for providing Water-Energy-Heat Nexus of a Rural Community
abstract: Freshwater scarcity around the world is a growing and challenging problem. The reverse osmosis (RO) plant offers the best results to overcome this problem, which provides freshwater. Many remote areas lack basic needs such as fresh water and electricity due to their geographical location. Thus, in this paper, a distributed generation (DG) microgrid is modeled, which acts as a vital source in powering the RO plant to provide freshwater needs and load demand of the rural community. Also, the thermal power of the hybrid renewable energy system (HREs) is used to dry tea leaves in the tea garden factory, providing jobs and boosting people's economic livelihood. The techno-economic feasibility study is done in Hybrid Optimization of Multiple Energy Resources (HOMER) software.

articleTitle: Elimination of Hot-Spot in a Photovoltaic Module using Protection Diode
abstract: Partial shading is a common phenomenon in the photovoltaic (PV) system and reduces maximum generated output power. In the efficient solar module shadowing effect, a relatively hot spot hinders improving the overall PV system. Bypass diode (BPD) and blocking diodes (BD) are two essential components to protect the PV module or array from unwanted heat loss. Light intensity is an essential parameter for PV power generation, and various levels of sun irradiance levels give the theoretical understanding of partial shading in the solar cell. In this paper, the current-voltage (I-V) and power-voltage (P-V) characteristics have been analysed in the case of shadowing cells with unshaded cells in Matlab software. Also, the output characteristics have been shown with and without BPD.

articleTitle: Rural Electrification Using Computer Vision and Wireless Sensor Networks
abstract: The procedure of supplying electrical electricity to rural and isolated locations is known as rural electrification. Rural towns are experiencing massive market imperfections as national systems fail to meet their electrical needs. when it comes to development regulations, the concept of a “smart city” has gained a lot of traction. The purpose of a smart city is to make better use of public resources and deliver better services to inhabitants while lowering operating expenses. In this research, smart street light applications are employed to create wireless sensor networks for smart cities, and they are also used to construct the networks. The street lights feature wireless sensor kits that gather information about temperature, humidity, and carbon dioxide levels to keep a watch on the environment. They also keep track of regional changes. The following is how it works: In addition, each sensor package includes a camera for monitoring environmental activity. A Raspberry Pi programming card was used to create the sensor kit. A sensor kit has been created specifically for this card. We stacked the XBee wireless modules on top of the sensor kit to make it wireless. The information is saved in a database. An interface is used to provide the data to the user.

articleTitle: FOFSE based Power Quality Improvement of 3-phase Solar Energy Conversion System
abstract: The solar PV generation system is critical for meeting the distribution end energy requirements. There were several difficulties experienced in transmitting energy from the source towards the load. The fundamental aim is to keep the power factor close to unity that may be accomplished by meeting the load's reactive power requirement. Harmonics are introduced into the system by non-linear load demand. The suggested FOFSE control is an excellent approach for resolving power quality issues due to the load, which is non-linear and linked at PCC. The FOFSE is utilized with in the system to recover the basic in phase element of the deformed grid voltage. Behaviour of the system is assessed on the MATLAB simulation software, and it has been discovered that even in aberrant grid conditions, the system meet these requirements to the standards specified in the IEEE-519 standard.

articleTitle: Video-Based Human Activity Detection
abstract: Human activity detection has become a prime research area in computer vision problem. There are many applications where human activity detection can be incorporated such as analyzing the video data which will help to monitor data generated by closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras. In this paper, a system is proposed which uses convolutional neural network along with incremental learning to detect different type human activities in videos. The proposed system is evaluated on benchmark dataset, KTH dataset.

articleTitle: Brain Tumor Classification via Optimal Feature Selection and Optimal Trained Neural Network
abstract: Brain tumor is a deadly disease with more casualty rates than surviving rate. Currently, with the arrival of technologies, it is turning out to be enviable to carry out automatic computer-oriented analysis of brain tumor images. Tumor segmentation and classification were the 2 vital tasks enclosed in the earlier works for brain tumor analysis. Even if numerous classification schemes were developed by the researchers, there exist several issues in reaching better accuracy. Here, this work intends to introduce a new approach that includes varied stages. At first, the features like “Contrast, Cluster shade, Energy, Cluster Prominence, Entropy, Variance, Correlation, Maximum Probability, Similarity, Sum entropy, Difference Variance, Skewness, Kurtosis, and Inverse Difference Normalized” are derived from the image of input. These characteristics are then optimally chosen via the SA- EHO model. Subsequently, an NN (optimized Neural Network) is utilized for detecting the tumors in brain images, in which the weights are tuned by a Self Adaptive EHO (SA-EHO). In the end, the upgrading of deployed scheme is confirmed regarding diverse metrics.

articleTitle: An Open loop time series ANN model for forecasting solar insolation for standalone PV applications
abstract: A standalone DC Microgrid comprising PV as a distributed generator has gained popularity as it gives a promising solution for pollution control and supplies increasing DC loads. The intermittent nature of PV gives rise to challenges in energy management. Hence a system that aids in making appropriate decisions in energy management is essential. In this regard, a system that forecasts solar insolation accurately is imperative to guarantee uninterrupted energy supply to the critical loads. The existing closed loop Artificial Neural Network model developed for predicting solar insolation is costly and complex. Hence, the authors propose an open loop time series Artificial Neural Network model that is simple and economical with comparable accuracy. Bayesian Regularization algorithm is recommended. The model's performance is validated by measuring the Root Mean Square Error and coefficient of Regression.

Author Keywords: time series open loop Artificial Neural Network

articleTitle: 2-D GMRT: GCD based Mapped Real Transform for 2-D Signals
abstract: Mapped Real Transform (MRT) is an evolving transform that was originally developed for frequency domain analysis of 2-D signals in the real domain. Elimination of redundant MRT coefficients and arrangement of unique coefficients in the form of an N × N matrix resulted in Unique MRT (UMRT), which was an improved version of MRT. However this type of placement offered a scattered arrangement of phase terms and posed problems in many applications. Analysis of visual representation of unique coefficients led to the development of Sequency based MRT (SMRT). However it is applicable only for cases where size of data matrices happen to be a power of 2. A new placement scheme, to overcome the drawbacks of UMRT and SMRT, that arranges the coefficients based on GCD values of frequency index with respect to size of the signal is proposed in this paper. This type of placement would be a generalized version of SMRT.

articleTitle: Adaptive Backpropagation Algorithm for Clustered Indoor Motion Planning
abstract: Grid based navigation is the simplest navigation methodology for unmanned ground vehicles (UGV) particularly for indoors. The grid map formation, grid cell occupancy, self-localization and avoiding obstacles in derived path are major considerations in navigation. This research work elaborate a new strategy of mobile robot navigation to goal point using an Adaptive Backpropagation tree based algorithm. For a confined stopping point like a charging station for an autonomous vehicles, this work provide minimal solution to reach that point. The path exploration begin from the stop point rather than the start point where robot is located. This backpropagation strategy implemented in real time scenario for its effectiveness. The simulation and experimental results gives the scope for robotic applications such as advance to stationary parking point or charging point.

articleTitle: Active 2D Sound Source Localization using a Sample DCNN Architecture & Encoding
abstract: This paper presents how to use raw audio data (multi-channel) to train a deep convolutional neural network in an end-to-end architecture to locate active auditory sources in space. It employs a revolutionary Sample DCNN architecture and encoding approach to encode the spatial coordinates of sources, allowing for end-to-end 2D source localisation. A Transfer Learning approach is employed to train the DCNN. Using clean voice data from the TIMIT database's dialect 8, we synthesise and produce anechoic and reverberant datasets. We map the model's predictions on a 2D plane to visualise them.

articleTitle: STATCOM Based Reactive Power Compensation in Grid Connected Solar System
abstract: This research paper proposes STATCOM based reactive power compensation on grid connected solar system and a comparative analysis of STATCOM and capacitor bank. STATCOM is utilised to mitigate reactive power in power system. For optimal power extraction from a solar PV panels, The solar photovoltaic panel system is connected to the grid through DC-DC step-up converter and grid tied PWM inverter. ANN based maximum power point tracking method is used to extract the maximum power from a grid-connected solar system by controlling the duty cycle of the DC-DC step-up converter. An ANN block is trained using a variety of irradiance and temperature data. The Pulse width modulation(PWM) method based three phase inverter is designed using a dq0 transformation-based control technique. This suggested system has been tested under various load conditions. The STATCOM based system were simulated in detail, and comparisons were made.

articleTitle: Evaluating Degradation resistance of Silicone Rubber Nanocomposites using Deep Learning Technique for outdoor high voltage applications
abstract: In this proposed work, the possibility of detecting of degradation resistance of silicone rubber nanocomposites using Deep Learning Techniques has been explored. The undoped samples of Room Temperature Vulcanised Silicon Rubber and samples doped with Silica (SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>), Boron Nitride (BN), Titania (TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>), were subjected to increasing high voltage stress using IEC 60112 till erosion occurred leading to degradation of the sample. The weight loss due to the degradation was calculated theoretically and ranked. A model was also developed in MATLAB in parallel using the deep learning network to predict the degree of degradation. The primary aim of the paper is to explore the workability of the proposed deep learning framework, in classifying the degree of degradation. A comparison of the calculated results with the predictions obtained through the deep learning network for validation of the developed model is also reported in the paper.

articleTitle: Security Access Control System Enhanced with Face Mask Detection and Temperature Monitoring for Pandemic Trauma
abstract: COVID-19 has affected the livelihood of millions around the world. Pass-infection of the virus between the personnel is a large threat factor. During this pandemic, it's mandatory to wear a mask to prevent the spread of the COVID19. Biometrics and face detection are commonly used to track individual employees' attendance but face recognition methods are ineffective because wearing mask obscures a portion of the face. This biometric can be a medium for the transmission of viruses. The proposed system implements COVID preventive measures such as mask detection and monitors body temperature. In addition, the proposed system checks for authorized persons using RFID technology and employs fingerprint verification application via individual mobile phones for attendance purposes. The system predominantly inspects presence of face masks, then keeps track of body temperature and ultimately controls the automatic door associated with it using RFID technology and android app based fingerprint recognition to allow access to people with authorization.

articleTitle: Effective method to reduce Covariate issues in gait-based human identification
abstract: Current research on gait-based human identification is increasingly interested in improving the performance of various existing gait recognition algorithms using various gait templates. However, the effectiveness of the existing gait template repre-sentation methods to tackle the influence of covariates condition need to be enhanced. An alternative method for reducing the effect of the covariates factor is proposed in the paper. The paper proposes integrating GEI (Gait energy image), a commonly used gait representation method, with GGMI (Gait gradient magnitude image), a Gaussian edge preserving technique for images. Subsequently, HoG(Histogram of Oriented Gradient) feature descriptor is used to extract features, followed by LDA (Linear Discriminant Analysis) is used for identifying different subjects. The experimental study is performed using CASIA-B dataset, the largest gait dataset with three variations, namely normal walk, clothing, and carrying conditions in this paper. We examine the effect of normal walking, clothing, and carrying conditions using the proposed method, using some existing CCR(Correct Classification Rate) evaluation methods. Experimental results show that the proposed method is effective against the factors that reduce the gait recognition performance with an average CCR of 73.33% for all the covariates.

articleTitle: Autonomous Ticketing System with Bus Health Monitoring
abstract: The purpose of this article is to make public transportation significantly more accessible and to boost its usage. The existing systems in the majority of developing countries lack a properly centralized system capable of harnessing the power of technology to create a seamless user experience. Thus, our goal is to automate the bus ticketing and boarding procedure by utilizing digital tickets and streamlining the process for commuters. Additionally, we intend to focus on emergency response by monitoring all bus health metrics such as engine temperature, emissions, and driver drowsiness and reporting them immediately to the appropriate authorities. We also intend to monitor accidents and report them automatically to the nearest hospital and police station. This work seeks to accomplish all of the above under a single massively scalable umbrella, taking into account all possible scenarios such as internet outage, sensor malfunction, and so on. We want to accomplish this by splitting the scenario into three facets: the commuter facet, the bus facet, and the administrative facet. The commuter aspect is a React-based web application that lets users to view all nearby bus routes and book one accordingly. And pick between automatic payment, which deducts the fare immediately upon boarding the bus, or traditional payment options. The bus aspect will be comprised of hardware views that will record driver sleepiness and bus health information using a variety of sensors and actuators, as well as a CV model, and transmit it in real-time to a database via a microcontroller.
