articleTitle: Classification of Brain Tumor Into Four Categories Using Convolution Neural Network
abstract: A Brain Tumor is a growth of abnormal cells in the brain which can cause discomfort and loss of function for some parts of the brain. The detection and classification of brain tumor using MRI Imaging is done manually by doctors and radiologists which is very time consuming and tedious task as well as the accuracy depends upon the human expertise. So, the use of computer aided technology such as Deep Learning becomes very necessary to overcome these limitations. Our proposed system used Deep Learning algorithm called CNN for automated detection and classification of brain tumor using MRI images into four major categories, Glioma, Meningioma, Pituitary Tumor and No-Tumor. Our dataset consists of 7,183 Brain MRI Images collected from different hospitals and few private scan centers in Mumbai, India. Out of 7,183 Brain MRI images, 5,712 images were used for training and 1,471 images were used for Test Dataset 1 and Test Dataset 2 contains 1,311 images acquired from online sources. Our proposed system has achieved 97.82% accuracy, 97.54% precision, 98.01% recall and 97.76% f1-score on the Test Dataset 1 while Test Dataset 2 achieved 98.70% accuracy, 98.59% precision, 98.66% recall and 98.61% f1-score.

articleTitle: Designing Hexagon, Triangle, Circle Shaped Microstrip Patch Antennas Using Coconut Coir Substrate
abstract: This paper aims to design low-cost Antennas using a number of commonly used shapes other than rectangle and extract the best results from them which can be used for wireless IoT based technologies. There is always a need for options in the realm of antenna design that help to reduce total production cost without sacrificing the performance. The FR4, Duroid, RO 4003 and Roger 4350 are the most commonly used antenna substrates, with FR4 being the most cost-effective. The nano cellulose from coconut coir can be employed as an alternative to low dielectric substrates due to its flexible nature, durable character and for being more favorable in terms of cost and environment. In this paper, three different shapes viz triangular, hexagonal and circlular of the microstrip patch antennas are designed by using coconut coir substrate and all these antennas can be prepared at much lower cost as compared to FR4 based antenna for 2.4 GHz operation.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Analysis Including Deep-Learning Predictions of a 1MW Grid-Connected Solar Photovoltaic Plant
abstract: The need for renewable energy sources is increasing because of a four-fold rise in energy demand due to the rise in the population and industrialization. The abundant nature of renewable sources has opened the doors to meet energy demands. The photovoltaic systems are showing a great impact on renewable energy penetration. Better design and performance evaluation in conjunction with certain power prediction techniques are required to use the PV power plants with greater efficiency. In this work, we have designed a 1MW ground-mounted and grid-interactive PV power plant in easy steps for better understanding by a normal person. Detailed estimates are made right from PV strings to the inverter. Past weather data from NASA is taken for estimation purposes. Performance analysis is done with PVsyst Software. PV Power prediction is done with BLSTM network. Finally, conclusions are drawn by mentioning the further use of artificial intelligence techniques in future works for more accuracy.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile Rectangular Dielectric Resonator Antenna with Partially Reflective Surface for 5G Applications
abstract: A Low-Profile Rectangular Dielectric Resonator Antenna (RDRA) with high gain and wideband is designed. The RDRA is excited by a microstrip stepped aperture slot on the ground plane. The swastika-shaped partially reflective surface (PRS) structure is loaded as a superstrate on the RDRA to enhance the peak of 10.24 dB. The proposed geometry offers impedance bandwidth from 3.15GHz to 5.88GHz suitable for 5G NR band applications.

articleTitle: Improved Edge Detection Approach to Tackle Edge Thickness and Better Edge Connectivity
abstract: Edge detection is substantial in helping us to pre-process any image for various applications from helping us to detect objects to detecting various medical conditions. The paper tackled one major shortcoming with the currently present system which is edge thickness. To improve there is an implementation of multiple thresholds instead of two thresholds generally used by techniques like that in Canny. The selected method solves multiple problems perfecting the handling of errors and more real to truth results. Our aim of refining the method helps us in better edge detection in images with low contrast as well as medical images like MRIs and X-rays.

articleTitle: Attention guided EEG based Game Genre Classification
abstract: Video games are ingrained in people of all ages and backgrounds demographically. The primary objective of a game is to amuse the player, and the designer's fundamental game design concepts have a direct impact on the player's enjoyment. In this paper, a framework is presented in which electroencephalography (EEG) is used for classifying the two-game genres - Action and Puzzle, based on player cognitive attention. The features used for game genres classification are frequency domain characteristics (i.e. band average power) and Sample Entropy derived from EEG signals of gamers. Based on the features it is observed that a player's brain activity significantly varies when interacting with the different game genres. The machine learning models - Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Neural Network (NN) is employed for classification. Conclusively both techniques effectually model the EEG signal recorded during game genres play. However, under an optimal selection of parameters, the Neural Network (NN) model outturn the highest possible accuracy of 98.35% as compared to the Support Vector Machine (SVM) which attained the utmost accuracy of 96.24%. It is also observed that Neural Network (NN) classifies the game genres more effectively in comparison with Support Vector Machine (SVM).
